_what: Which shape each §8 `S` cell takes, decided by RFC-2026-022 §3's test and recorded here rather than argued in each migration's header.
_why_this_file_exists_before_any_entry: RFC-2026-022 names this file, and four batches are about to classify cells at the same time. If each created it, the merge would be a four-way conflict over a file whose whole purpose is to be one list — so it is created once, empty, with the rules that read it.
Empty is a claim: no §8 `S` cell has been classified yet. The rules below make that claim checkable rather than merely true today.

_shape.cell: the §8 row and column this entry classifies, quoted from the access matrix
_shape.table: table name created by a migration in db/foundation/migrations/, schema-qualified as `app.<name>` or `private.<name>`; an unqualified name means `app`
_shape.why: which half of RFC-2026-022 §3's test the STATEMENT falls on, in a sentence someone can disagree with
_shape.batch: the migration batch that classified it

_not_in_effect: RFC-2026-022 is approved and NOT IN EFFECT: measured 2026-09-08, the only member of app_worker is postgres, which bypasses RLS. A batch classifies its cells here; it does not write a service policy until §7 holds.
_what_batch_110_classified: Batch 110 classifies one cell here: §8.3's "Raw token/webhook SELECT", which RFC-2026-022 §3's own table assigns to batches 110 and 131 and calls DISCOVERED. 131 owns the same cell for the payment inbox and adds its own row; the register keys on (cell, statement), so two rows for one cell on two tables is the shape §5/1 describes rather than a duplicate.
_a_private_table_needed_the_rule_to_say_: The `table` field was documented as "unqualified table name in the app schema", and this cell's table is in `private` — §3.1 puts "raw webhook" there by name and §14's gate checklist requires it not be exposed. The rule could not express the entry it was written to receive. It now accepts a schema-qualified name and resolves an unqualified one to `app`, which changes no verdict for a cell in `app` and is asserted in test-kits/db/foundation-contract.test.mjs in both directions.
_what_batch_132_classified: Nothing, and the absence is a decision rather than an omission. RFC-2026-022 classifies §8 `S` CELLS, and §8's four matrices contain no row for an entitlement resolution and no row for a read of the plan catalog: §8.4's two metering rows (usage/quota summary SELECT, usage ledger INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) are batch 061's and are already classified or already `N`, and §8.3's two billing rows (Billing/subscription SELECT, Plan/payment action) are batch 130's. Batch 130's own header says it: "§8's four matrices contain no row for a plan catalog anywhere." So there is no cell for batch 132 to classify, and inventing a `cell` value would be a claim about the access matrix made in a lint file -- batch 061's sentence about its own reservation and quota bucket, unchanged. This note exists because batch 130's isolation case service-sees-zero-plan-entitlements says the service policy on app.plan_entitlements is "owed to that batch", meaning 132: it is not owed, because RFC-2026-022 sanctions a service policy for an §8 `S` cell and for nothing else, and a policy TO app_worker on a table with no matrix row would be a permission no cell grants. app_worker keeps its SELECT grant and no policy there. tests/db/identity/identity-isolation.test.mjs holds the negative -- no cell in this file names batch 132 -- so the claim is checkable rather than only written.

cells.why: The statement a processor issues is "the next unprocessed delivery", and it contains no workspace term because WHICH workspace is what reading the row resolves. Under RFC-2026-022 §3's operational test, adding the confinement term to its WHERE does not narrow the same work — it turns "the unprocessed webhook" into "the unprocessed webhook of a tenant I already knew", which is not the work. The schema says the same thing: private.meta_webhook_inbox.workspace_id is NULLABLE, because a delivery arrives before anything knows whose it is and resolution can fail, and batch 110's apply-time block refuses a later NOT NULL.

cells.cell: §8.4 Usage ledger INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (`S/N`) — the `S` half, which is the INSERT
cells.why: The statement's workspace is an INPUT and not an output. RFC-2026-022 §3 already classes this cell CARRIED, giving the reason 'a reservation is made against a known quota'; applying §3's own operational form to the STATEMENT gives a stronger one. Add `and workspace_id = (select nullif(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid)` to this INSERT's WITH CHECK and it still writes the same row, because CTR-USG-001 makes attribution.workspace_id a REQUIRED property of the envelope and composes the dedupe_key with that same workspace as its second segment -- 061_metering.sql then constrains the key to start with the row's own workspace, so the workspace is something the row says twice before any policy reads it. Nothing here is a claim about the confinement term being a boundary: RFC-2026-022 §5/4 measured that app_worker can set the setting the policy would read, so the term is containment against defects in the service's own code and never tenant isolation of the service path. NO POLICY IS WRITTEN: the decision is approved and NOT IN EFFECT (§5/8, and the `_not_in_effect` note above), so this row classifies the cell and authorises nothing. §8.4's UPDATE and DELETE half is `N` for the service too, which is why this table has one entry and not three; app.usage_reservations and app.quota_buckets have none at all, because §8 has no row for either in any of its four matrices and inventing a `cell` value would be a claim about the access matrix made in a lint file.

cells.cell: §8.4 Notification insert/delivery state | N | N | N | N | N | S
cells.why: The workspace is an INPUT. §8.4's other notification row marks "Own notification SELECT/mark read" `O`, so an inbox row cannot be addressed at all without knowing whose it is -- and app.notifications carries user_id NOT NULL beside workspace_id NOT NULL, both in the INSERT's own VALUES list. Applying RFC-2026-022 §3's operational form: add `and workspace_id = (select nullif(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid)` to the WITH CHECK and the statement still addresses the same work -- "insert a notification for this recipient in this workspace" is unchanged, because the server resolved both before forming it. Nothing here discovers a workspace by reading, which is the half of §3's test that would make it DISCOVERED. RFC-2026-022 §3's own table classifies this cell for batch 051 as CARRIED with the reason "recipient and workspace are inputs"; this row is that classification checked against the statement rather than accepted from the table.

cells.cell: §8.4 Notification insert/delivery state | N | N | N | N | N | S
cells.why: The delivery-state half of the same cell, classified separately because RFC-2026-022 §7.2 keys the register on (cell, STATEMENT) and never on the table alone -- the asset-hard-purge row in §3's table is BOTH shapes for exactly that reason. The statement is `update app.notifications set delivery_state = ..., delivery_failure_class = ... where id = $1`: it names one row by its id, and that row's workspace came back with it from the send that produced the report. Adding the confinement term to its WHERE changes nothing about which row it addresses. Contrast batch 050's claim on app.jobs, which is DISCOVERED because `for update skip locked` on the next due row has no workspace term to add without changing what the work is; a delivery report is written about a notification the service already holds, not selected across tenants by age or readiness.

RFC-2026-022 §3's operational test, applied to the statement rather than to the table. The statement a billing webhook processor issues is `select … where processed_at is null and dead_lettered_at is null and next_attempt_at <= now() order by received_at for update skip locked` — the next receipt nobody has resolved. Add the confinement term `and correlation_workspace_id = (select nullif(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid)` and the work CHANGES: "the next unprocessed receipt" becomes "the next unprocessed receipt of a tenant I already knew". On this table it is worse than on a queue, because the column the term reads is NULL on exactly the rows the processor exists to resolve — §8.3 of the Stripe billing contract initialises `correlation_workspace_id` to null in its own minimum field list, since a provider event arrives outside any session and the workspace is what reading it resolves. So the workspace is the statement's OUTPUT, the cell is DISCOVERED, and per RFC-2026-022 §5/5 app_worker holds grants and NO POLICY on this table permanently rather than pending. Batch 131 writes no service policy: the decision is NOT IN EFFECT (§5/8 — measured 2026-09-08, the only member of app_worker is postgres, which bypasses RLS), and the broker §5/6 names has no identity to grant EXECUTE to. The confinement term is containment against defects in the service's own code and never tenant isolation of the service path (§5/4); no case, comment or assertion in batch 131 cites it as the latter.

cells.cell: §8.2 Research run/source/evidence INSERT | N | N | N | N | N | S — the run
cells.why: RFC-2026-022 §3's operational test applied to the statement, and applied rather than looked up: §3's own table classifies cells for 050, 051, 061, 110, 120, 131 and the asset purge and does not name §8.2's research row at all, so batch 070 derives the shape instead of citing a verdict. The statement a research worker issues is `insert into app.research_runs (workspace_id, business_profile_id, page_context_profile_id, brief, created_by) values (...)`. Add `and workspace_id = (select nullif(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid)` to its WITH CHECK and it writes the same row: the workspace is what the REQUESTER asked about, resolved by the server before the work was enqueued -- CTR-TEN-001's trust boundary is "Server-resolved only after membership and Workspace→Business→Page relation validation; client-supplied context is untrusted input" -- and it sits in the statement's own VALUES list beside a business_profile_id that must agree with it through a composite foreign key into app.business_profiles. Nothing here discovers a workspace by reading, which is the half of §3's test that would make it DISCOVERED. Contrast batch 050's claim on app.jobs: `for update skip locked` over the next due row has no workspace term to add without changing what the work IS. NO POLICY IS WRITTEN: the decision is approved and NOT IN EFFECT (§5/8 and the `_not_in_effect` note above), so this row classifies the cell and authorises nothing. The confinement term is containment against defects in the service's own code and never tenant isolation of the service path (§5/4); no comment, case or assertion in batch 070 cites it as the latter.

cells.cell: §8.2 Research run/source/evidence INSERT | N | N | N | N | N | S — the source
cells.why: The same cell one level down, classified separately because RFC-2026-022 §7.2 keys the register on (cell, STATEMENT) and never on the table alone, and derived by applying RFC-2026-022 §3's operational test rather than by citing a verdict -- §3's own table does not name §8.2's research row. The statement is `insert into app.research_sources (workspace_id, business_profile_id, research_run_id, source_uri) values (...)` -- "record that run R cited this URL". R was resolved when the work was claimed, and the source's workspace_id and business_profile_id are copied from R and held to it by a composite foreign key into app.research_runs (workspace_id, business_profile_id, id), so the workspace is something the row says twice before any policy reads it. Adding the confinement term to the WITH CHECK changes nothing about which row it writes. CARRIED.

cells.cell: §8.2 Research run/source/evidence INSERT | N | N | N | N | N | S — the evidence
cells.why: The third statement §8.2's `S` names, against a source the same worker has just written, and classified by applying RFC-2026-022 §3's operational test rather than by citing a verdict -- §3's own table names 050, 051, 061, 110, 120, 131 and the asset purge and does not name §8.2's research row at all. Its workspace_id and business_profile_id are copied from that source and held to it by a composite foreign key, so the confinement term is redundant rather than restrictive and the cell is CARRIED. THE MAP CARRIES THREE ENTRIES FOR THIS BATCH AND NOT FIVE: §8.2's `S` names the run, the source and the evidence and stops, and §8 has no row anywhere for inserting a research SNAPSHOT or a research SUGGESTION -- a run proposes a suggestion (§4's ERD) and a snapshot is COPYRIGHT-3 material §9.1 gives no service cell for. Where a document is silent the cell is denied, and inventing a `cell` value for either would be a claim about the access matrix made in a lint file (061's sentence, unchanged). Neither table carries a policy, and app_worker holds grants and none, so both refusals stay attributable to row level security.

cells.cell: §8.2 Asset hard purge | N | N | N | N | N | S — the workspace-closure purge
cells.why: RFC-2026-022 §3's table names this cell for batches 100 and 160 and calls it BOTH; this row is the CARRIED half, checked against the statement rather than copied from the verdict. §11.4 is a workspace deletion lifecycle and its step 7 purges "tenant content, research, ASSETS", so the statement a closure worker issues is `update app.asset_versions set object_key = null, purged_at = now(), status = 'purged' where workspace_id = $1 and purged_at is null and id = any ($2)`. The workspace is already in the WHERE as a parameter -- it is the SUBJECT of the operation, named by the closure request that started it -- so adding `and workspace_id = (select nullif(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid)` is redundant rather than restrictive and the statement writes the same rows. CARRIED. The operation is `update` and not `delete` because §9.3/11 of the object storage lifecycle contract makes the purge an update of deleted_at/purged_at and §11.5 requires the row to survive as a redacted status; no role holds DELETE on any table batch 100 creates. The id list is a list of EXACT ROWS: CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS.md requires an approved immutable manifest of exact object keys and forbids a recursive prefix delete, and asset_versions_object_key_names_one_object refuses a stored key that is a wildcard, a traversal or a folder. NO POLICY IS WRITTEN: the decision is approved and NOT IN EFFECT (§5/8 and the `_not_in_effect` note above -- the only member of app_worker is postgres, which bypasses RLS), so this row classifies the cell and authorises nothing. The confinement term is containment against defects in the service's own code and never tenant isolation of the service path (§5/4); no comment, case or assertion in batch 100 cites it as the latter.

cells.cell: §8.2 Asset hard purge | N | N | N | N | N | S — the retention sweep
cells.why: The DISCOVERED half of the same cell, on a different table and a different statement, which is precisely why RFC-2026-022 §7.2 keys this register on (cell, statement) and never on the table alone. §10's ASSET-ORIGINAL gives "Trash 30 วัน; block purge if referenced/hold" and §7.4 of the asset design moves `Trash --> PurgeQueued: พ้น retention และไม่มี reference`. The statement a sweep issues is `select ... from app.assets where deleted_at is not null and purge_after <= now()` and then the purge that follows it -- it contains no workspace term because WHICH workspace is what reading the row resolves. Apply §3's operational form: add the confinement term and the work CHANGES, from "the assets whose Trash window has expired" to "the expired assets of a tenant I already knew", which is not a sweep; the sweep exists because nobody named a tenant. The workspace is the statement's OUTPUT. DISCOVERED. Per §5/5 a discovered cell gets NO POLICY permanently rather than pending, and is performed through a SECURITY DEFINER broker owned by a role that is not a path -- `app_queue`, which §7.1/4 requires to exist with exactly one pinned function and which DOES NOT EXIST. NO POLICY AND NO BROKER IS WRITTEN: RFC-2026-022 is approved and NOT IN EFFECT (§5/8 and the `_not_in_effect` note above -- the only member of app_worker is postgres, which bypasses RLS, and a broker function has nobody to grant EXECUTE to), so this row classifies the cell and authorises nothing. app_worker holds `update (current_version_id, purge_after, updated_at)` on app.assets and no policy, so the refusal stays attributable to row level security. THE SWEEP IS THE SHAPE THE PREFIX RULE IS MOST DANGEROUS IN and that is recorded rather than left: a statement selecting by age across tenants is one `like $1 || '%'` away from a recursive prefix purge, §9.3 forbids that as a กฎบังคับ and requires an approved snapshot of exact keys first, and no table in §6's registry owns such a snapshot -- an open blocker on WP-0A-DB-00, not something this classification closes.

_what_batch_100_classified: Batch 100 classifies ONE cell here TWICE, and it is the only cell in RFC-2026-022 §3's table the RFC itself calls BOTH. §8.2's "Asset hard purge | N | N | N | N | N | S" is named in §3's table against batches `100` and `160`, with the paragraph under it: "Driven by §11.4's workspace closure it is CARRIED -- the workspace is the subject of the whole operation. Driven by a retention sweep it is DISCOVERED -- the sweep selects by age across tenants and learns the workspace from the row. A cell may have both shapes, because the class attaches to the statement." §7.2 keys this register on (cell, STATEMENT) and never on the table alone, which is exactly what two rows for one cell is for. BOTH ARE `update` AND NEITHER IS `delete`: §9.3/11 of the object storage lifecycle contract makes the purge "อัปเดต `deleted_at/purged_at` แบบ idempotent" and §11.5 confirms it from the support side ("visible to support as redacted status"), so the row survives as a redaction and NO ROLE HOLDS DELETE anywhere in batch 100. THE OTHER THREE TABLES GET NO ROW: §8 has no cell anywhere for creating an asset version, a rights record or a content asset link, and inventing a `cell` value would be a claim about the access matrix made in a lint file (061's sentence, kept by 070 and 080). app_worker holds grants and no policy on all four, so every refusal stays attributable to row level security. AND THE MANIFEST GAP IS NOT CLASSIFIED HERE BECAUSE IT IS NOT AN §8 QUESTION: §9.3 requires production deletion to work from an approved immutable snapshot of exact object keys and no table in §6's registry owns one; that is an open blocker on WP-0A-DB-00 and not a shape this register can express.
